references.text: Abraham served butter and milk to his guests, showing the richness of God's blessing, as described in Deuteronomy 32:14.
It speaks of the finest oil, wine, and grain as firstfruits to the Lord, paralleling the rich gifts mentioned in Deuteronomy 32:14.
Bashan is mentioned as a fertile area known for its cattle, relevant to the reference to 'rams from Bashan' in the original text.
God feeds His people with the finest wheat and honey from the rock, a parallel to the richness described in Deuteronomy 32:14.
It mentions butter and honey as signs of abundance and blessing, similar to the theme in Deuteronomy 32:14.
Ezekiel describes rams, lambs, goats, and oxen from Bashan, directly paralleling the animals mentioned in Deuteronomy 32:14.
The cows of Bashan are used as an image, linking to the reference about Bashan's cattle in Deuteronomy 32:14.
Jacob's blessing mentions washing clothes in wine and grapes, parallel to 'the blood of grapes' in Deuteronomy 32:14.
Isaiah describes a meal with rich dishes and good wine, similar to the abundance of food and drink in Deuteronomy 32:14.
